title: C# Questions & Answers - Destructors in Class
sourceFile: Destructors in Class - C# Questions & Answers - Sanfoundry.html
description: This section of our 1000+ C# multiple choice questions focuses on destructors in class in C# Programming Language.

questions.question: Which operator among the following signifies the destructor operator in C#?
questions.explanation: In C#, a destructor (also called a finalizer) is declared by prefixing the class name with the tilde (~) operator.

questions.question: Which method is called by clients of a class to explicitly release unmanaged resources (like network connections or file handles) when the object is no longer required?
questions.explanation: The 'Dispose()' method, part of the IDisposable interface, is used for deterministic release of unmanaged resources, as opposed to the non-deterministic nature of the Garbage Collector.

questions.question: Which method has the same name as the class (prefixed with ~) and is used to clean up an object when the instance is being reclaimed by the Garbage Collector?
questions.explanation: A destructor (finalizer) is used to perform any necessary final clean-up when a class instance is being collected by the garbage collector.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Garbage Collection (GC) in .NET are correct?

options.text: There is one garbage collector per program running in memory
The Garbage Collector is a shared service of the CLR for all managed applications
Setting an object reference to null makes it eligible for garbage collection
Both B and C are correct

questions.explanation: The GC is a service provided by the Common Language Runtime (CLR). To allow an object to be collected, you should remove all references to it, such as by setting them to null.

questions.question: Which operator is used to manually free memory in C#?
questions.explanation: C# does not have a 'delete' or 'free' operator for managed memory. Memory is automatically reclaimed by the Garbage Collector.

questions.question: Select the WRONG statement about destructors in C#:

options.text: A class can have only one destructor
Destructors cannot be inherited or overloaded
Destructors can have access modifiers (like public) or parameters
Destructors are called automatically by the GC

questions.explanation: Destructors cannot have access modifiers (public, private, etc.) and cannot take any parameters.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: The constructor runs first (8 + 2.5 = 10.5). When the application ends or GC collects the object, the destructor runs (8 - 2.5 = 5.5).

questions.question: What is the return type of a destructor in C#?
questions.explanation: Destructors do not have a return type, not even 'void'.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: A destructor cannot have an access modifier (like 'public'). This causes a compile-time error in C#.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?

options.text: Code executes but prints nothing in Main

questions.explanation: The destructor calculates the volume (4 * 5 * 9 = 180) and prints it when the object is finalized by the Garbage Collector.
